summary.oneLiner: Lloyds Luxuries Limited is the India operator of the British heritage grooming brand Truefitt & Hill, running a network of premium gentleman's barbershops alongside an e-commerce business in premium grooming products.
summary.business: The Company operates premium men's grooming and lifestyle services in India under the globally recognised heritage brand Truefitt & Hill, delivering salon/barbershop services through highly skilled professionals at premium locations. Alongside its physical salon network it sells premium grooming products through leading online marketplaces and a direct-to-consumer platform, building an omnichannel presence. Its stated customer proposition is service quality, personalised experience and a trusted international brand for the premium grooming consumer.

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- India - premium grooming and personal care consumers
- Key metropolitan and high-growth Indian markets (locations named: Ameya One in Gurugram; Bandra and Worli in Mumbai)
- Online marketplaces and direct-to-consumer digital channel in India

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India's premium grooming and personal care industry is described as having strong long-term growth potential, supported by rising disposable incomes, increasing urbanization, greater consumer awareness, premiumization trends and a growing preference for organized branded services
- Consumers are increasingly seeking superior service quality, personalized experiences and trusted international brands, which management frames as a significant opportunity for established premium players
- Demand-side driver stated for the year: healthy customer demand, growing brand acceptance and consistent performance of both retail and digital channels; strong customer retention and word-of-mouth referrals driving higher footfalls
- Digital and e-commerce expected to remain an important growth driver, with online marketplaces and the D2C platform complementing the physical retail network
- Margin lever stated: improved operating leverage, prudent resource utilisation, cost optimisation and continuous improvement in procurement, inventory and analytics are expected to enhance productivity and improve margins
- Cost headwind flagged: currency fluctuation, particularly depreciation of the Indian Rupee against the Pound Sterling, resulted in higher input costs during FY 2025-26
- Management's stated view that strategic investments made over the years in brand equity, footprint and customer relationships have established the foundation for the next phase of growth

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Measured, disciplined expansion of the premium retail footprint towards approximately 50 Truefitt & Hill locations across key metropolitan and high-growth Indian markets, with each new location evaluated through a disciplined investment framework emphasising location quality and sustainable returns
- Build the digital and e-commerce channel as a distinct growth driver - strengthening presence across leading online marketplaces, enhancing the direct-to-consumer platform and using digital engagement to deliver a seamless omnichannel experience that complements the physical network
- Brand building as a stated key strategic priority - curated marketing initiatives, premium lifestyle collaborations, exclusive partnerships and signature brand experiences to reinforce heritage, authenticity and premium positioning
- Invest in human capital through structured technical training, leadership development programmes, performance-based incentives and employee ownership initiatives, on the view that service excellence is the cornerstone of the luxury grooming business
- Strengthen operational efficiency through technology adoption, digital transformation, process optimisation and data-driven decision-making across procurement, inventory management, CRM and business analytics
- Maintain focus on sustainable and profitable growth, prudent capital allocation and operational excellence rather than growth at any cost, while sustaining premium customer-experience standards
- Scale the operating platform through disciplined resource allocation, improved procurement, enhanced inventory management, better utilisation of existing infrastructure and standardised operating processes
- The routed text discloses no dividend recommendation, dividend policy, buyback, debt-reduction plan or credit rating. Stated intent is qualitative: the Board says the Company 'will continue to focus on sustainable and profitable growth, prudent capital allocation and operational excellence', and that each new retail location is evaluated through a disciplined investment framework emphasising long-term value creation, location quality and sustainable returns - i.e. reinvestment into the store network and the digital platform rather than distribution. Stated NIL / negative disclosures relevant to the balance sheet: the Company has not extended any corporate guarantee on behalf of any other company during the year; it has not made any one-time settlement with any lender; no IBC application or proceeding exists; particulars of Section 186 loans and investments are cross-referenced to the notes to the standalone financial statements and are not reproduced here. Equity is being expanded modestly through ESOPs (2,71,210 shares allotted to the ESOP trust in FY2025-26; a new ESOP Scheme - 2026 authorises up to 11,04,000 further options). As on 31 March 2026, 2,41,34,873 equity shares - about 100% of issued, subscribed and paid-up capital - were held in dematerialised form. Shares are listed on the NSE SME platform, and Para C of Schedule V of the LODR (the corporate governance report) is not applicable to the Company by virtue of Regulation 15(2). A special resolution at the 13th AGM (31 August 2026) seeks approval to increase the Managing Director's remuneration with effect from 1 April 2026 for one year, in a no-profit / inadequate-profit situation and above the Schedule V ceiling.

Expansion is described as 'measured' and 'disciplined', with each new location evaluated through a disciplined investment framework emphasising long-term value creation, location quality and sustainable returns. moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Globally recognised heritage brand - the Company introduced the timeless British heritage of Truefitt & Hill to India and describes a 'globally recognized heritage brand' as a competitive advantage
- Loyal and growing customer base with high repeat business - management attributes growth to strong customer retention, client loyalty and positive word-of-mouth referrals
- Highly skilled grooming professionals and premium service standards cited as the true hallmarks of the brand
- Expanding omnichannel presence combining a physical salon network with e-commerce/D2C reach
- Scalable, asset-light operating model with a disciplined investment framework applied to each new location
